text.p: Pen pictures of the probable Bayern Munich team for Sunday's German first division clash with 1860 Munich:
Oliver Kahn. Goalkeeper. Age 27. Germany's second-choice keeper who is ambitious to make a career in the national team. A big man who dominates the penalty area with both his stature and loud voice.

Lothar Matthaeus. Libero. 36. Germany's most capped player with 122 international appearances and a former World Cup captain. His international days now look over. He did not go to England with Euro 96 squad. Slower than in his heyday but still a player who can turn a match with a piece of skill.
Markus Babbel. Defender. 24. Euro 96 player who was tipped to be Juergen Kohler's successor as main man-to-man marker in national team but who has yet to match the Dortmund player's consistency.

Thomas Helmer. Defender. 32. German international who operates mainly as a man marker for Bayern. He can also slot easily into the libero role. A calming influence on the side and one of its undisputed leadership figures.

Mario Basler. Midfielder. 28. Joined from Werder Bremen at start of season. The German international has promised a great deal in recent seasons but injuries have often hindered his progress. One of the country's most gifted players but his comments in public often get him into trouble.
Christian Nerlinger. Midfielder. 24. One of Bayern's rising stars who has been at the club since 1987 and who fits into the team well alongside the bigger names.

Dietmar Hamann. Midfiedler. 23. Another of the versatile rising stars, who was at the centre of a scare earlier in the season when he collapsed at home with a suspected stroke. Later examination revealed only a minor problem and Hamann has made a complete recovery.

Christian Ziege. Wing back. 25. Left-sided German international who has risen to prominence with a string of impresive displays for both Bayern and the national side. Will join AC Milan at the end of this season.

Alexander Zickler. Midfiedler/forward. 22. Former Dynamo Dresden player came under fire for lack of sharpness in front of goal when he was thrown into the team because of injuries two seasons ago but has matured into an intelligent player.

Juergen Klinsmann. Forward. 32. Germany's captain and most well-known player has rarely managed to produce his best form for Bayern and has announced he will leave the club at the end of the season. The former Tottenham player can still turn a game with a flash of brilliance, however.

Ruggeiro Rizzitelli. Forward. 29. Former Italian international had problems settling into the Bayern side when he joined from Torino at the start of the season. But he has been in brilliant form in the second half of the season, scoring goals himself and setting up chances for others.
